editorial:
Imagine you are stepping into a dark, dusty mansion where the walls feel like they are closing in on you. You meet a man who is terrified of his own home and his sick sister, who seems to just float through the hallways. Since this was a student project, the whole thing has a strange, dream-like feel that makes you feel uneasy. It does not rely on jump scares, but instead uses shadows and creepy silence to get under your skin. You will feel the tension building as the house starts to feel like a living thing that wants to trap everyone inside.

What really works here is how the director uses light and dark to make everything look spooky without spending much money. The acting is a bit stiff, but that actually makes the characters feel more robotic and weird, which fits the mood. If you like old-school horror that focuses on a creepy mood, you should definitely give this a try.
endingExplained: At the end, the tension finally snaps. The sister, who was thought to be dead, comes back in a scary way. As the house begins to physically break apart, the characters are swallowed up by the ruins. The whole building literally collapses into the lake, sinking everything beneath the water. It shows that the family curse was too strong to beat, and the house takes everyone down with it in a final crash.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves old gothic stories and creepy houses.
